pageInfo.subtitle: Master slides and glissando to add smooth, expressive transitions between notes.
pageInfo.heroDescription: Slides are one of the most expressive techniques available to guitarists. From subtle position shifts to dramatic glissando sweeps, mastering slides adds a vocal quality to your playing that connects notes in a way picks alone cannot achieve.

items.text: Maintain consistent finger pressure while sliding
Slide on the fingertip, not the pad, for cleaner tone
Keep the sliding finger close to the fret wire
Use your ear to judge arrival pitch accuracy
Start with short slides (1-2 frets) before longer distances
Practice both ascending and descending slides equally
Work on hitting the target note precisely
Combine slides with hammer-ons and pull-offs for legato lines

exercises.title: Two-Fret Ascending Slides
exercises.description: Pick the starting note, then slide your finger up two frets while maintaining pressure on the string. The second note should ring out clearly from the slide momentum alone. Practice on each string.

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Pick only the first note. The slide should produce the second note with full volume and sustain. If the second note is quiet, increase finger pressure during the slide.

exercises.title: Two-Fret Descending Slides
exercises.description: The reverse of the previous exercise. Pick the higher note and slide down two frets. Descending slides require slightly more pressure to maintain volume since you're working against string tension.

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Descending slides can lose volume easily. Apply slightly more pressure into the fretboard during the downward motion. The arrival note should be as clear as the starting note.

exercises.title: Long-Distance Slides
exercises.description: Slide across larger distances (5+ frets). This requires smooth arm movement and consistent finger pressure throughout the entire slide. Practice landing on the target fret precisely.

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: For long slides, move your entire arm, not just the fingers. Keep even pressure throughout. Aim to stop exactly on the target fret, not before or after.

exercises.title: Slide Into and Out of Notes
exercises.description: Slide into a note from a few frets below (grace note slide) and slide out by releasing pressure as you slide away. This adds a vocal-like quality used extensively in blues, country, and rock.

notation.title: Grace Note Slides
notation.staveTitle: Slide Into Notes from Below & Above

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Grace note slides should be quick - the starting pitch is heard briefly before landing on the target note. Blues and rock players use this constantly for expression.

exercises.title: Pentatonic Slide Licks
exercises.description: Apply slides within the A minor pentatonic scale. Use slides to shift between positions 1 and 2 of the pentatonic pattern. This creates smooth, connected runs that sound more musical than jumping between notes.

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Use slides as connectors between pentatonic positions rather than lifting and shifting. This is how David Gilmour, BB King, and Eric Clapton achieve their smooth legato sound.

exercises.title: Double-Stop Slides
exercises.description: Slide two notes simultaneously on adjacent strings. This creates rich, harmonized slide sounds. Press down firmly with one finger barred across two strings and slide both together. Common in blues, rock, and country.

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Use your ring or pinky finger barred across two strings. Apply even pressure on both strings. Both notes should slide at the same speed and arrive together.

items.title: Perfecting Your Slides
items: Think of slides as vocal scoops - they should sound musical, not mechanical
Vary slide speed for different effects: fast for energy, slow for drama
Use string lubricant if slides feel scratchy on wound strings
Practice slide accuracy by checking intonation at the arrival fret

items.title: Musical Applications
items: Blues players use slides to mimic vocal inflections
Country players use pedal steel-style slides on double stops
Rock soloists use slides to connect pentatonic positions seamlessly
Jazz players use chromatic approach slides into target notes
